system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — BUYER LEGAL ADVICE**  
**Project Kestrel — Seller Mark-up vs. Playbook**  

---

### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY  
The Seller’s “updated SPA positions” and Disclosure Letter **depart materially from the playbook on every core protection**. They attempt to lock in our *fallback* positions (without authority), collapse the fundamental/title regime into the general cap, extend limitations to fraud, impose broad deemed disclosure, and leave Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, and title evidence unresolved. **Do not treat this as a “fair and balanced package.”** A detailed mark-up and a formal push-back letter are required before any further negotiation round.

---

### CLAUSE-BY-CLAUSE DEPARTURES & REQUIRED PUSH-BACKS  

| # | Issue | Seller Position | Playbook Requirement | Departure Severity | Required Action |
|---|-------|-----------------|----------------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| **1** | **General Cap** (Cl. 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8M | 25% / AUD 6M (starting); 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority (none given) | **Critical** — Seller proposes our *unauthorised fallback* as opening bid. | Reject 20%. Insist on 25% / AUD 6M. Document that no authority exists for 20%. |
| **2** | **De minimis / Basket** (Cl. 12.2) | De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k (excess only) | De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k (first-dollar recovery once exceeded) | **Critical** — 5× higher thresholds + “excess only” shifts material risk to Buyer. | Red-line to AUD 5k / AUD 50k first-dollar. |
| **3** | **General Claims Period** (Cl. 12.3/13) | 18 months; “all Claims subject to same limitations unless expressly stated” | 24 months (starting); 18 months only with Amelia Frost approval (none). Fundamental/Title: separate regime, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. | **Critical** — Seller compresses time *and* tries to drag fundamental claims into general regime. | Hold 24 months. Insert express carve-out: fundamental/title claims **not** subject to general cap, basket, de minimis, knowledge bar, or 18-month limit. |
| **4** | **Fundamental / Title Warranties** | “Subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity” | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. | **Critical** — Title/capacity protection eviscerated. | Reject categorically. Draft standalone fundamental-warranty clause with 100% cap, 6+ years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge qualifier. |
| **5** | **Fraud / Wilful Misconduct Carve-out** (Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply to **all Claims of any nature** | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance. Non-waivable. | **Critical** — Seller attempts to limit liability for fraud. | Insert express carve-out clause (non-waivable) covering fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct. |
| **6** | **Disclosure** (Sch. 7 / Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2) | General disclosure of **entire data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers, public registers** | **Require specific fair disclosure**; reject whole-data-room, public-register, prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **High** — Blanket disclosure shifts diligence risk to Buyer. | Delete general disclosure clauses. Require schedule of *specific* disclosures with page/bates references. |
| **7** | **Buyer Knowledge** (Cl. 8.3) | No claim for matters Buyer/advisers “had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records” | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier: named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity. | **High** — Constructive knowledge from data room = deemed disclosure by another name. | Strike Cl. 8.3. If Seller insists on knowledge qualifier, limit to *actual* knowledge of named Buyer individuals (list to be agreed) and carve out title/capacity/fraud/indemnities. |
| **8** | **Bluefen Consent** (Cl. 3/6.3) | “Reasonable endeavours”; consent treated as satisfied **on delivery of counterparty’s written consent** (no evidence conditions satisfied) | **Effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied BEFORE Completion**. Reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for material customer. | **High** — Consent-on-delivery without condition satisfaction = completion risk. | Amend condition precedent: (a) Bluefen written consent *and* (b) certified copy/evidence that Cl. 11.3 conditions met. No “reasonable endeavours” fallback. |
| **9** | **Riverlark Facility** (Cl. 2/7) | Release “to be provided **following Completion**” (~AUD 3.2M outstanding) | **Current payout + direct repayment from Completion funds + effective security releases**. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. | **High** — Post-completion discharge without undertaking leaves Buyer exposed. | Require payoff at Completion from funds flow. If Seller insists on post-completion, demand irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval (neither present). |
| **10** | **Employee Bonuses (DD-005)** | AUD 420k conditional bonuses “not separately itemised in funds flow”; “matter for Seller”; on-costs unaddressed | **Specific line item or Seller-funded**; funds flow must not silently exclude AUD 420k + triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super). | **High** — Silent exclusion = purchase price leakage. | Insert dedicated funds-flow line: “Seller Bonus Amount AUD 420k + on-costs” payable by Seller or deducted from price. Confirm on-cost quantum. |
| **11** | **Ironquay IP Indemnity** (Cl. 11.1) | Limited to SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open); “considered adequate” | **Broaden narrow indemnity**, preserve SOW3 cure. AUD 180k not independently verified. | **Medium-High** — Narrow indemnity may not cover IP ownership/third-party claims. | Expand indemnity to cover (i) IP ownership/encumbrance, (ii) third-party infringement, (iii) SOW3 cure costs. Require independent verification of AUD 180k status. |
| **12** | **Export/Privacy Incident (DD-006)** | “Preliminary operational matter not expected to be material” | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. **Assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.** | **Medium** — Seller pre-judges materiality; investigation incomplete. | Add covenant: (a) preserve all logs/evidence, (b) continue investigation pre/post-Completion, (c) monthly written updates, (d) Buyer right to assume conduct of notification/defence. No admission of breach. |
| **13** | **Sandbar Renewals (AUD 330k)** | “Ordinary-course operating costs” | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Low-Medium** — Alignment on “no auto debt,” but scope/avoidability unclear. | Request termination/avoidability analysis. Reserve right to adjust working capital if not ordinary course. |
| **14** | **Tax / IP Warranties** | “Settled under the general regime above” | **Remain OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. | **High** — Seller tries to fold Tax/IP into capped, short general regime. | Confirm Tax/IP warranties **separate**, uncapped (or higher cap), longer limitation, outside general basket/de minimis. |
| **15** | **Title Evidence** | “Evidenced by Company share register at DD-012” | **Independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence. DD-012 is internal, not independent. | **High** — Internal register ≠ independent proof. | Require: (a) ASIC certified extract, (b) solicitor’s title opinion, (c) no-encumbrance certificate, (d) board/shareholder resolutions authorising sale. |
| **16** | **Disclosure Letter Reservations** (§§2–11) | Multiple “NOT included / NOT repaid / NOT verified / NOT characterised” statements | Playbook requires *positive* resolution pre-Completion (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff, Ironquay payment proof, bonus funding, incident investigation). | **High** — Disclosure Letter confirms *open* items Seller treats as “disclosed away.” | Convert each open item into a **condition precedent** or **specific indemnity** with funds-flow mechanism. Do not accept disclosure as cure. |

---

### TOP 5 “MUST-WIN” ITEMS
=== END ADVICE ===
